action.action: Jensen Huang이 외국 정보기관의 공작 대상이 되었다는 보도와 관련해 독립이사 위원회가 외부 독립 법률고문의 지원을 받아 조사를 개시

key_facts: **NVIDIA 이사회는 Jensen Huang이 외국 정보기관의 표적이 되었다는 최근 보도를 근거로 독립 조사를 개시**
독립이사로 구성된 위원회가 외부 독립 법률고문의 지원을 받아 조사를 감독
이사회는 국가안보 및 기밀정보가 침해되었다고 믿을 근거가 없다고 밝힘
Jensen Huang은 조사를 전적으로 지지하며 협조하기로 약속
**이사회는 Jensen Huang과 경영진에 대한 신뢰를 표명**하고 추가 업데이트를 제공할 예정
summary_data.why_matters: **NVIDIA CEO를 둘러싼 외국 정보기관 관련 의혹은 반도체·AI 기술 패권 경쟁 속 국가안보 민감성을 부각시키며, 투자자·규제당국의 신뢰에 영향을 줄 수 있는 사안**이다. 조사 결과에 따라 NVIDIA의 수출통제·대중국 정책 등 지정학적 리스크 관리 역량이 재평가될 수 있다.
summary_data.subject_angle: **NVIDIA는 핵심 리더십의 신뢰성 문제가 회사의 전략적 포지션과 투자자 신뢰에 미칠 영향을 조기에 관리하기 위해 선제적 투명성 조치를 취하고 있다.**

Nvidia Board of Directors Is Investigating Jensen Huang
Statement from NVIDIA Board of Directors

cards.body: The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.

key_facts: **뉴욕타임스 조사 결과 New Matrix와 Maginfra의 사무실 주소가 빈 사무실이었고 인근 관계자들도 해당 기업을 알지 못함**
New Matrix 설립자 Li Bin은 제재 대상 사모펀드 Wise Road, Entity List 등재 기업 New H3C Semiconductor, 중국 정부 소유 Tsinghua Unigroup과 연관
Maginfra는 2023년부터 제재 대상인 Inspur와 인력·특허·지배구조를 공유하는 것으로 의심됨
Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology 경영진은 중국군 관련 기업에 컴퓨팅 자원을 판매한 Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group 창립자와 연관
**트럼프 대통령이 2025년 4월 수출을 금지했다가 판매액의 25% 환수 조건으로 번복했으며, 베이징의 승인 지연으로 첫 H200 출하까지 8개월 이상 소요됨**
summary_data.why_matters: 미 상무부가 수출 라이선스 심사를 형식적으로 처리할 경우 **군사용 전환 위험이 있는 중국 기업에 첨단 AI 칩이 유입될 가능성**이 커지며 이는 대중(對中) 수출 통제 체계 전체의 신뢰성을 흔든다. 동시에 바이두·BYD·테슬라 상하이 등 정상 기업과 유령 기업이 같은 승인 목록에 섞여 있어 NVIDIA의 고객 실사(due diligence) 책임 논란으로 확산될 수 있다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 **중국 매출 재개를 위해 미 상무부 승인에 의존**하고 있지만, 승인 기업의 실체 검증 부실이 드러나면서 추가 규제 강화나 라이선스 재검토 리스크에 노출될 수 있다.

cards.body: An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them. According to The New York Times , these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military. This news has revealed concerns that the U.S. Department of Commerce is simply rubber-stamping GPU export license applications instead of scrutinizing each one for potential links to Beijing. “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” former China director for the White House National Security Council Liza Tobin told the publication. Many of these approved companies include well-known entities like Baidu, BYD, Tesla Shanghai, as well as ZTE , which has previously been blacklisted from the U.S. market, Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance. However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra. The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces. The New Matrix website also reportedly did not contain any information about its owners or its history, although public company records reveal that it was founded by Li Bin, who, along with two other primary owners, are connected to Wise Road, a Chinese private equity firm sanctioned by the U.S. for helping Beijing acquire sensitive chip technologies. Furthermore, Mr. Li chairs Tsinghua Unigroup, a tech conglomerate partly owned by the Chinese government, and owns New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, which has also been added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List for cooperating with the Chinese military. Maginfra, on the other hand, is suspected of being linked to Inspur, which Washington has b lacklisted since 2023 for supporting the People’s Liberation Army, with both companies sharing personnel, patents, and a similar government ownership structure. These two firms aren’t listed as the final users of Nvidia’s AI chips, though. Instead, they’re supposed to assemble them into AI servers, which would then be forwarded to a final user, although it’s unclear who their customers are. Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links. Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology’s executives are reportedly related to the founder of Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group, a data center operator that has sold compute capacity to Chinese military contractors. related.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces bipartisan congressional scrutiny over reported China spy link

cards.body: Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle are ramping up calls for congressional investigations into reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia's board announced Sunday it is opening an independent investigation into Huang's involvement with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that the U.S. has suspected of helping China circumvent artificial intelligence chip sales prohibitions. In a memo to Nvidia staff on Sunday, Huang disclosed he had been intimate with the woman, but the affair was not mentioned in the board's statement. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating, the board said. "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the board said in its statement. "Today's news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," the company told CNBC in a statement. Lawmakers have been calling for an investigation into the relationship and are also questioning what the Trump administration knew about it. "The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I'm convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn't corrupt," Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., posted on X on Saturday. "Congress will investigate and get answers." Coons is in line to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when his party takes control of the chamber in January. Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday asking him to sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18, a day after the company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings. "Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People's Republic of China's] access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the GOP lawmakers wrote in a letter to Huang. Policymakers in the Trump administration received a memo last spring with intelligence identifying Alice Huang as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and revealing her relationship with Nvidia's chief executive, the Times first reported on Friday. Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the memo's creation, the Times reported Sunday, citing people briefed on the matter. The State Department and the White House did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment. When asked by the Times whether Huang would appear before lawmakers to discuss the matter, Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo declined to comment. "Our chief executive has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed," Mr. Rizzo said in a statement to the Times. cards.body: I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence. Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American. My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy. Jensen

related.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits affair with alleged Chinese spy, board to investigate
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to affair with alleged Chinese spy as company board launches investigation

cards.body: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an affair with a woman accused of spying for the Chinese government. Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) was an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based IT and cloud company currently under investigation for smuggling Nvidia GPUs into China. Last year, US intelligence agencies surveilling Megaspeed and Alice Huang discovered a relationship with Jensen Huang, and believe she sought to illicit information from him as well as access to the chips. Megaspeed, which has bought more than $2 billion in Nvidia hardware, has denied involvement in chip smuggling. When news of the then-unspecified relationship was published by the New York Times earlier this month, Nvidia's Huang called the story "groundless speculation," and claimed that "our relationship, our interactions, have been related to Megaspeed, and it was completely normal and not unusual." A week later, after further reporting on the investigation, Jensen Huang admitted to the affair. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," he said in a letter to staff. "Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. "To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust." Jensen Huang, perhaps the figure most singularly critical to the current AI boom, said that he remained "fully committed" to Nvidia. His comments made no reference to the allegations of spying. Nvidia's board said that it was initiating "an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The company added that it “has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised; the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.” Jensen Huang, who has often appeared alongside US President Donald Trump at AI events, has openly lobbied to loosen trade restrictions with China to increase sales of Nvidia hardware in the mainland. On Thursday, Congressional Republicans wrote to Jensen Huang requesting a closed-door briefing about the incident. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” said Michigan Rep. John Moolenaar, who is also chairman of the House Select Committee on China. “It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk."

Nvidia launches investigation into CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy

cards.body: Nvidia has opened an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy. U.S. intelligence agencies have expressed concerns that the woman, Alice Huang, who is affiliated with a cloud company and an Nvidia customer called Megaspeed, has been passing information to Beijing, according to reports in The New York Times and the Financial Times. Huang told Nvidia staff in an email on Sunday that he had an affair with the woman and that Nvidia's board of directors had opened an independent investigation into the spying allegations. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote in the message. "I am deeply sorry." An Nvidia spokesperson said that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption. In a statement, the Nvidia board said it would investigate the allegations that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," Nvidia's board said in a statement. Read Huang's email to Nvidia employees and the company board of directors' statement here. The allegations come as Nvidia has become the center of a trade dispute between China and the U.S. as AI is seen as increasingly critical to national security. The U.S. restricts exports of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to China, though it has approved exports of certain older, slower models. Megaspeed, which Ms. Huang is affiliated with, has been accused of helping restricted Chinese companies acquire Nvidia AI chips. Nvidia representatives previously said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls. Nvidia's Huang has pushed for broader AI chip exports to China, saying it is better for the U.S. if the world uses and builds on American technology. He has also aligned with President Donald Trump on American artificial intelligence policy and its infrastructure buildout. In his note to staff, Huang said he was "proud and grateful" to be an American. Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday asking him to sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18. Nvidia reports third-quarter earnings on Nov. 17 and will hold a major conference in Washington, D.C., at the end of the month.

Nvidia opens investigation: Was CEO Jensen Huang target of foreign intelligence?

cards.body: Nvidia said on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”. The New York Times reported in October that Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence that Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump downplayed the revelations about Huang, who is an influential adviser to the president on artificial intelligence, saying: “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it.” Trump also brushed off a question about whether he now regrets not acting on the intelligence when he was briefed on it, and suggested that he would be happy to take Huang with him on a trip to Asia next week. “I haven’t heard he’s done anything wrong,” Trump said. “He dealt with somebody. But, you know, so does everybody else.” Republican lawmakers have expressed more alarm, asking Huang to give the Houseforeign affairs and intelligence committees a closed-door briefing next week on Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” and his relationship withAlice Huang or Huang Le, an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed, who is of no relation to the Nvidia CEO. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her. Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources. The company’s board said in a statement on Sunday that, while it has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information. “The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.” Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added. Axios reported on Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full responsibility for his actions. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” Huang said in the draft email also seen by Reuters. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report. The Times reported on Sunday that a memo drafted by US secretary of state Marco Rubio circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring, citing intelligence that the businesswoman who had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s ministry of state security. headlines.body: Nvidia on Sunday said it has opened an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies said is a Chinese spy. "Today's news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," the company told CNBC in a statement. Below is a staff email from Huang obtained by CNBC and a statement released Sunday about the investigation from Nvidia's board of directors. Staff email from Huang: [From:] Jensen Huang [To:] Employees Subj.: A message to our company Nov. 8, 2026 To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence. Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American. My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy. — Jensen Statement from Nvidia's board of directors: The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.

headlines.body: Ukraine is developing a new class of combat robots designed to operate inside underground gas pipelines, where Russian troops have repeatedly attempted to bypass frontline defenses, United24Media reports. The project, disclosed by Ukraine's 2 nd National Guard Corps, Khartiia, involves modifying unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) to perform reconnaissance and combat missions in spaces too narrow for conventional military machinery. Notably, the work is being carried out by specialists from the corps’ Lava Unmanned Systems Regiment, following Operation Veles — an underground assault that saw Ukrainian soldiers advance more than 15 kilometers through pipeline infrastructure near Kupiansk. Khartiia says the operation killed more than 100 enemy soldiers and resulted in over 30 captured, although those battlefield figures have not been independently verified. The commander of Lavas ground robotic system battalion, identified by the callsign ‘Matematyk’, said the project addresses a category of warfare that requires a different approach from conventional battlefield robotics. “There is a very long list of tasks that need to be accomplished to fight underground and counter the enemy underground. This is a new class of technologies and challenges that we will have to confront,” he said. The machines are being adapted from existing groundrobots ,rather than developed as conventional surface vehicles. They must be compact enough to navigate narrow pipelines while retaining the ability to carry out military assignments . Most commercially available underground machinery, meanwhile, is designed for construction, drilling, and tunneling — not combat. As of now, Khartiia is already developing several robotic systems to address those limitations, with the broader objective of sending machines into dangerous underground environments where soldiers would otherwise have to conduct reconnaissance, confront enemy positions, clear positions, or clear out themselves. “War is already underground, and it will expand. The question is how we adapt to this war,” Matematyk said. The project follows unusual battlefield developments near Kupiansk, where Ukrainian forces used the same underground infrastructure that Russian troops have previously exploited to infiltrate behind Ukrainian defensive positions. During Operation Vels, Ukrainian soldiers moved through a gas pipeline measuring approximately 1.2 meters in diameter, according to a report by Ikrainska Pravda. The confined passage made movement and close-range firefights particularly,with Ukrainian troops having little-to-no room to maneuver. Russia had previously used the pipeline network beneath the Oskil River to move soldiers toward Ukrainian-held territory. The Ukrainian battlefield monitoring group ‘Deepstate' reported an earlier Russian infiltration attempt in September 2025.
